blocks.value: Without generics, a container holds `Object` and every retrieval needs a cast:

List rawList = new ArrayList();        // raw type
rawList.add("hello");
rawList.add(42);                       // nothing stops this

String s = (String) rawList.get(1);    // compiles, ClassCastException at run time
With generics, the mistake never reaches run time:
**Generics move an entire category of error from run time to compile time**, which is the same argument as Lesson 18 made for enums, applied to types rather than values.
